The story

Christopher Ward was founded in 2004 by Mike France, Peter Ellis, and Christopher Ward after a boat trip on the River Thames. They launched in 2005 as the first online-only luxury watch retailer, aiming to provide high-quality, Swiss-made watches at lower prices by avoiding traditional retail markups. The first models were the C5 Malvern Automatic and C3 Malvern Chronograph, and the brand quickly gained a following within online watch communities. A significant turning point came in 2014 when the company merged with its Swiss manufacturing partner, Synergies Horlogères. This merger enabled the launch of their first in-house movement, the Calibre SH21, a chronometer-certified movement with a five-day power reserve, which was a major development for a British watch brand. The brand's offerings have since expanded to include a variety of popular lines. The C60 Trident Pro 600 is a key part of their dive watch collection, which has been a cornerstone of the brand since 2009. More recent additions include the versatile C63 Sealander Automatic and C63 Sealander GMT, introduced in 2021 as “go-anywhere, do-anything” sports watches. The C65 Dune Shoreline, a more retro-styled field watch, further showcases their design diversity. Today, Christopher Ward continues to operate with a blend of British design and Swiss manufacturing, headquartered in Maidenhead, UK. Co-founder Christopher Ward departed the business in 2020, but the company has continued to grow, releasing innovative and popular models. They have expanded from a purely online model to include physical showrooms and have gained recognition for both their value proposition and their technical achievements in watchmaking.
